candidates.summary: Harrison Chase (LangChain) published an X article, "The five components of building a 'company harness'", describing how LangChain runs three internal agents (GTM Agent, OpenSWE, Content Studio) and the primitives every team converged on: living in Slack, per-tool identity, two-tier memory, sandboxed code execution, and scheduled or event-triggered runs.
facts: The three agents: GTM Agent (monitors email and new qualified leads, sends daily briefs, answers account questions, runs outbound), OpenSWE (drafts PRs and runs code review over all PRs), Content Studio (drafts blogs, images, PowerPoints and videos in LangChain's style).

Chase calls identity "the thorniest and trickiest problem": each agent mixes on-behalf-of-user actions with fixed credentials, per tool. OpenSWE opens PRs under the requesting user's GitHub handle but reviews code in the background as its own GitHub app.

GTM Agent's email tools act on behalf of the user and are available only in DMs, not in shared channels; Content Studio posts to the company Twitter account with fixed credentials, and only a whitelisted set of users can invoke that.
Memory has two tiers, global and per-user, and the agent decides which tier a fact goes to; Chase says this is the least explored area.
Agents run outside the sandbox and connect to it to execute code, using the secret proxy on LangSmith Sandboxes to reach authenticated services.
A large share of runs are scheduled or event-triggered rather than invoked by a person; in one example the GTM agent created its own cron to send a daily brief.
Agents can "break out" of a human Slack thread into their own thread; for large review backlogs LangChain built a custom UI instead of Slack.
All three are built on Managed Deep Agents, on top of the open-source Deep Agents harness.

related.name: Add identity to Managed Deep Agents

candidates.summary: Perplexity added /impeccable, an open-source skill built by Paul Bakaus (@pbakaus), to the skills marketplace in Perplexity Computer. Aravind Srinivas says it lets users build interfaces that don't look like AI-generated slop.
facts: Perplexity's @AskPerplexity account says the skill reviews an interface and fixes what a designer would flag, checking layout, type, contrast and accessibility.
Tasks that use /impeccable are free through October 31, up to 5,000 credits per user.

candidates.summary: a16z's Charts of the Week says power is one of the AI buildout's biggest bottlenecks and US factory capacity to make electrical equipment has shrunk since 2019 while prices rose.
facts: US factory capacity since 2019, per a16z: communications equipment +110%, semiconductors +77%, computers +16%, electrical equipment -9%.
a16z says electrical equipment prices are up 69%, the biggest jump of the four categories.

candidates.summary: a16z says GPUs are still renting ahead of a standard 6-year depreciation schedule, and most of the gap opened after April, when token demand took off.
facts: Rental price vs. depreciation schedule, per a16z: H200 +143%, B200 +111%, RTX PRO 6000 +73%, H100 +54%, A100 +9%.
The post quotes a16z's earlier chart on GPU rental rates rising year to date (seen in the 2026-10-23 evening run).

candidates.summary: Security researcher @log4j, who posted on Oct 21 that they had a root shell on new Samsung TVs via zero-days, says OpenAI banned their account for reverse-engineering work. The claim spread on Saturday through a post by @yacinemtb and a quote from Nous Research promoting its Hermes Agent.
facts: @log4j: "i have never used openai to exploit or find vulnerabilities, only local reverse engineering which tripped daybreak."
@log4j says the ban cost them $500 and "a bunch of banked resets", and posted two screenshots.

@log4j's original Samsung TV post (Oct 21) says they kept getting weirdly targeted ads, found the firmware AES-encrypted, used zero-days for a root shell, and "discovered PRIVACY HORROR"; it reached a Hacker News front page ("Root shell on Samsung TV").
@yacinemtb's post framing it as "Person who is reverse engineering his tv gets banned from OpenAI" had 12,508 likes when read.
Nous Research quoted it: "Hermes Agent gives you control".
This run found no OpenAI statement on the ban; the claim rests on the user's own post and screenshots.

related.name: Hacker News: Root shell on Samsung TV
